title: build-caching
description: Learn about build-caching. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Build caching dramatically speeds up development and CI/CD processes by reusing previous build results. By caching dependencies, intermediate build artifacts, and final outputs, you can reduce build times from minutes to seconds.
Why Build Caching Matters

Modern build processes involve transpilation, bundling, optimization, and asset processing. Without caching, every build performs all these operations from scratch, wasting time and computational resources.

data.title: Build Time Impact
data.code:
Without Build Caching:
- Initial build: 5 minutes
- Small change rebuild: 5 minutes
- Dependency install: 2 minutes
- Transpilation: 2 minutes
- Bundling: 1 minute

With Build Caching:
- Initial build: 5 minutes (same)
- Small change rebuild: 30 seconds (90% faster)
- Dependency install: cached (instant)
- Transpilation: cached (instant)
- Bundling: cached (instant)

Time Savings:
- Development: Hours saved per day
- CI/CD: Faster feedback, reduced costs
- Team productivity: More iterations, faster delivery

data.text: Types of Build Caching
1. Dependency Caching
Cache node_modules and other dependencies to avoid reinstalling them on every build. This is the biggest time saver for most projects.

data.title: Dependency Caching in CI/CD
data.code:
# .github/workflows/build.yml
name: Build
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      
      - name: Cache node_modules
        uses: actions/cache@v2
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-node-
      
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

data.text: CI/CD Caching Strategies
Implement comprehensive caching in CI/CD pipelines to reduce build times and infrastructure costs. Use cache keys that reflect dependencies to ensure cache invalidation when needed.

data.title: Comprehensive CI/CD Caching
data.code:
# .github/workflows/comprehensive-cache.yml
name: Build with Cache
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      
      # Cache node_modules
      - name: Cache Dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v2
        with:
          path: |
            node_modules
            ~/.npm
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-deps-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-deps-
      
      # Cache Next.js build
      - name: Cache Next.js Build
        uses: actions/cache@v2
        with:
          path: |
            .next/cache
            .next/standalone
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-nextjs-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-nextjs-
      
      # Cache webpack
      - name: Cache Webpack
        uses: actions/cache@v2
        with:
          path: .webpack_cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-webpack-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
      
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci
      
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build
      
      - name: Test
        run: npm test

data.text: Cache Invalidation
Ensure caches are invalidated when dependencies change. Use appropriate cache keys that include file hashes or version numbers.

data.title: Cache Key Strategies
data.code:
Cache Key Strategies:

1. File Hash-Based
   key: deps-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
   - Invalidates when dependencies change
   - Most common and reliable

2. Version-Based
   key: deps-v${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
   - Invalidates on version bump
   - Requires version extraction step

3. Combination Strategy
   key: ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}-node-${{ hashFiles('.nvmrc') }}
   - Multiple sources for cache key
   - More specific, reduces false hits

4. Restore Keys
   restore-keys: |
     ${{ runner.os }}-node-
   - Fallback to broader cache key
   - Provides partial cache hit

Best Practices:
- Include file hashes for dependencies
- Include OS/architecture for cross-platform builds
- Use restore-keys for partial cache hits
- Monitor cache hit rates
- Periodically clear old caches

data.text: Remote Caching
Remote caching services like GitHub Actions Cache, GitLab Cache, or self-hosted solutions allow sharing cache across different runners and machines.

data.title: Popular Remote Caching Services
data.code:
Remote Caching Services:

1. GitHub Actions Cache
   - Integrated with GitHub Actions
   - 10GB storage per repository
   - 7-day retention for unused caches
   - Free for public repositories

2. GitLab CI Cache
   - Integrated with GitLab CI
   - Configurable retention
   - Distributed across runners
   - Included in GitLab tiers

3. TeamCity Build Cache
   - Self-hosted option
   - Highly configurable
   - Enterprise features
   - Requires TeamCity license

4. nx (Nx Cloud)
   - Distributed caching
   - CI integration
   - Smart invalidation
   - Free for open source

5. Self-hosted (Redis, S3)
   - Full control
   - Requires maintenance
   - Custom implementation
   - Potentially cost-effective at scale

data.title: Cache Size Limits
data.text: Most caching services have storage limits. Monitor cache sizes and implement cleanup strategies to avoid hitting limits. Use compression and cache only essential artifacts.
Cache Performance Monitoring
Monitor cache hit rates and build times to ensure caching is providing value. Track metrics to identify caching issues and optimization opportunities.
